claim.why_it_matters: The 'Lydian:' label from the top of PDF page 1188 is concatenated onto Lycian's range line; Lydian's range '10920-10939' opens the next page with no label.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed against both rendered pages. PDF page 1217 (printed folio 1187) ends its script list with two lines, 'Lycian:' then '10280-1029C', followed immediately by the page footer '(c)ISO/IEC 2023 1187'. No 'Lydian:' token appears anywhere on page 1217 -- I read the rendered glyphs directly. PDF page 1218 (printed folio 1188) opens, under the running head 'ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)', with 'Lydian:' then '10920-10939', then 'Mahajani:'. The markdown at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 49263 reads '10280-1029C Lydian:' as a single line, and the page-1218 section (after the anchor, the '## Page 1218' heading and the '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' running head) opens with the bare line '10920-10939'. Both halves of the claim are quoted accurately. I considered rejecting this as page-break furniture or line wrapping, since no token is lost and source order is preserved (Lycian: / 10280-1029C / Lydian: / 10920-10939). I reject that defence. This table's entire semantic content is the label-to-range binding: each script name on one line, its code-point ranges on the next. The transcription destroys two bindings at once -- it appends a foreign label to Lycian's range line, so 'Lycian: 10280-1029C Lydian:' reads as if Lycian's range list ends in a script name, and it strands '10920-10939' with no owning script at the top of the next page. A line-based reader or parser of the markdown cannot recover that 10920-10939 belongs to Lydian without knowing that page furniture was mis-inserted. That is a change in what the text asserts, not merely how it is laid out. The defect is systematic, not a one-off. Grepping for a range line ending in a glued 'Name:' token finds 18 instances across the script-range tables, each at a page boundary: lines 40182 (Ahom), 40235 (Buhid), 40403 (Kaithi), 40454 (Linear_B), 40506 (Miao), 40558 (Old_Italic), 40610 (Rejang), 40772 (Buhid), 40824 (Gunjala_Gondi), 40876 (Khojki), 40928 (Mongolian), 40981 (Sharada), 49030 (Brahmi), 49087 (Deseret), 49207 (Kannada), 49263 (Lydian, this claim), 49319 (Multani), 49374 (Old_Turkic), 49431 (Sinhala). Every one is the same failure mode and every one leaves an unlabelled range line opening the following page.
verdict.corrected_description: Confirmed, with one refinement to the framing. No text is missing or invented -- all four tokens survive in source order. The precise defect is twofold: (a) the newline separating page 1187's last range line from page 1188's first label was dropped, gluing 'Lydian:' onto '10280-1029C'; and (b) the page-1218 boundary furniture (anchor, '## Page 1218', running head) was inserted one token late, i.e. after 'Lydian:' instead of before it. The consequence is exactly as claimed: Lycian's range line is polluted with a foreign label and Lydian's range '10920-10939' opens page 1218 unlabelled. This is not an isolated page-1217 defect -- it is a recurring page-boundary transcription fault affecting 18 sites in the Unicode script-range tables (markdown lines 40182, 40235, 40403, 40454, 40506, 40558, 40610, 40772, 40824, 40876, 40928, 40981, 49030, 49087, 49207, 49263, 49319, 49374, 49431), and should be fixed as a pattern rather than per page.
